prompt: A $13$-ft ladder leans against a wall with its foot $5$ ft from the base of the wall. How high up the wall does the ladder reach, in feet?
hint: The wall and the ground meet at a right angle. Decide which side of the triangle the ladder is before using the Pythagorean Theorem.

hints.text: The wall and the ground meet at a right angle. Decide which side of the triangle the ladder is before using the Pythagorean Theorem.
The ladder is the hypotenuse, so $c = 13$ and one leg is $5$. Solve $5^2 + b^2 = 13^2$ for the height $b$.
$b^2 = 169 - 25 = 144$, so $b = 12$ and the ladder reaches $12$ feet up the wall.

explanation: The wall meets the ground at a right angle, so the leaning ladder is the hypotenuse with $c = 13$.
Putting the known leg into the Pythagorean Theorem gives $5^2 + b^2 = 13^2$, which is $25 + b^2 = 169$.
Subtracting $25$ gives $b^2 = 144$, so $b = 12$ and the ladder reaches $12$ feet up the wall.

alternativeExplanations.title: Why subtract instead of add
steps: When you are hunting the hypotenuse you add the squares; when the hypotenuse is already known you subtract.
Sanity check: $12$ is shorter than the $13$-ft ladder, which is exactly what a leaning ladder should do.
